Please request a human review of the importance decision for TK-83975C.

Our wording “left locked on” may have made this sound like an unusual equipment failure. The submitted hardware uses the manufacturer's ordinary hold-down ring for continuous rinsing. Turning the sprayer off requires disengaging that control and allowing the spring-return trigger to close while controlling the suspended head.

There is more specific evidence of occupational relevance than the general cleaning duties cited in our original context:

- [EPA WaterSense](https://www.epa.gov/watersense/pre-rinse-spray-valves) reports that about one million U.S. food-service establishments use pre-rinse spray valves to rinse dishes. This supports widespread use of this particular equipment in commercial dishwashing.
- [T&S's exact B-0107-J-SWV product page](https://www.tsbrass.com/products/parts-accessories/spray-valves/B-0107-J-SWV) lists the hold-down ring and industrial-kitchen application. Its [foodservice catalog, page 8](https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/mid-city.com/resources/T_S_B_0665_BSTR_Catalog.pdf) describes a hold-down ring for continuous use in the same pre-rinse product family.
- [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/food-preparation-and-serving/food-preparation-workers.htm) reports 908,500 food-preparation-worker jobs in 2025 and includes cleaning equipment and dishes among their duties.

These sources establish equipment prevalence and the intended control function; they do not directly count workers who disengage the ring, so we are not claiming they independently prove the 500,000-worker threshold. Could a human reviewer reconsider whether ending continuous rinsing with the manufacturer's normal control constitutes a regular operation within commercial dishwashing work?

This request concerns the existing submitted task; no code or scope changes are proposed.

Please request a human review of the decision for TK-SM6ETU.

Two points are fair. The README links the Jetson, Delta fan and Orion guard CAD but does not state their licence terms. The files are downloaded at build time and not redistributed, but the terms should still be stated. Also, our demo reaches the offcut's exposed end with one grasp and pull, so the motion itself is less distinctive than our framing suggested.

What we ask a person to weigh is the constraint around that pull. The fan is powered and stalled by the offcut. The score is 0 if any finger or tool enters the blade region while the rotor is powered or coasting. The debris must be released in the tray with the hand clear. Full credit needs forward rotation above 4,000 RPM for 10 s afterwards. So the robot must choose whether to isolate power at the rocker, extract without entering the blade envelope, and then verify the repair. The fan is a user-fitted part of this board: NVIDIA documents its 4-pin header with tachometer input ([user guide](https://developer.nvidia.com/embedded/learn/jetson-nano-2gb-devkit-user-guide)). We think servicing the computer that runs a robot without touching live blades is ordinary robot-hardware maintenance. We have no source on how often such fans foul, and we don't claim one.

If reopened, we would:
1. Replace all three CAD models with self-made geometry built from the published datasheet dimensions, or state each licence if it permits this use.
2. Seat the offcut's end below the guard rings so it must be worked out through the 4.25 mm wire gap with the supplied pliers, not grasped directly.

Please request a human review of the decision for TK-GHB9F4.

Two criticisms are fair. The 0.5 mm vertical tolerance to the hidden support can't be checked with simple tools, and we have no source for that number. The reset also doesn't explain how to make a repeatable 3 mm salt grain or trap it on a real HT-120.

On importance, we believe the difficulty is robotic rather than diagnostic. The display already shows the fault at the start (−12.08 g with the pan empty). Everything after that is manipulation on a live 0.01 g sensor:
- lift the pan off its support without pressing on it;
- free a 3 mm grain from the rim gap;
- reseat the pan so it no longer touches the case;
- place the 100 g weight centred, release it with the hand 20 mm clear, then remove it without disturbing the pan.

Any robot contact during a reading voids it. A palm-supported control and a held-weight control both score 0. Pressing zero without the repair reads 59.43 g for the 100 g weight. Dream-1 scored 0. Removing the pan for cleaning and testing the balance afterwards is standard manufacturer procedure ([Mettler Toledo ME-T manual](https://www.mt.com/dam/P5/labtec/17_Miscellaneous/UM_ME-T_en.pdf), maintenance table and section 5.2, printed pp. 19–20).

If reopened, we would:
1. Drop the 0.5 mm pose condition. The released zero / 100 g / zero readings (±0.05 g) would serve as the load-path check, plus a visible check that the pan is seated with no rim contact.
2. Replace the salt with a 3 mm steel ball, which is a standard part and does not crush. It would be placed at a marked rim position with a written lift-place-reseat reset procedure.
